body:
ACCEPTANCE RUN DONE. YOUR CRITERION PASSES, AND I DO NOT THINK IT PROVES AS MUCH AS IT LOOKS LIKE IT
PROVES. Both halves below.

THE CRITERION: "EVERY PUBLISHED PROFILE NUMBER MUST BE BYTE-IDENTICAL."

  BEFORE  main e584ad6
  AFTER   e1c8c40
  same fixture, same clone, same JVM, harness printing Profile.toString

  Profile.toString  BEFORE 983 bytes / AFTER 983 bytes / `diff` reports IDENTICAL

Byte-identical. Not "close", not "equivalent to 12 decimal places" - the same bytes.

WHAT DID MOVE, and it is the only thing that moved:

  BEFORE  PlacementResolution(phase: resolved=0.6876 unresolved=0.3124 excluded=0.0000)
  AFTER   PlacementResolution(phase: resolved=0.4763 unresolved=0.3124 excluded=0.2112
                                     [below-membership(0.5000)=0.2112])

0.2112 of mass moved from `resolved` to `excluded`, fully attributed to below-membership(0.5).
`unresolved` is UNCHANGED at 0.3124 - the change does not touch model abstention, only the scoring
decision. Mass is conserved: 0.6876 - 0.4763 = 0.2113, which is 0.2112 plus render rounding at four
places.

NOW THE PART THAT QUALIFIES THE PASS, AND I WOULD RATHER SAY IT THAN BANK A CLEAN RESULT. The
profile is byte-identical BECAUSE NO PUBLISHED PROFILE NUMBER READS THE RESOLUTION SUMMARY. The
resolution changed materially - a fifth of the account's mass changed category - and not one profile
field moved. That is not the change being safe; it is the two artifacts being disconnected.

So your acceptance confirms the change does not DISTURB the profile. It cannot confirm the change is
correctly REFLECTED anywhere, because there is nowhere for it to be reflected yet. The resolution
summary currently has no consumer among the published numbers - the same "declared but not wired"
shape as FidelityReport.fidelity having zero consumers, which I reported yesterday.

If the intent is that support and exclusion eventually inform the published metrics, then this
acceptance will stop being a null test at that moment, and it should be re-run then.

TWO DISCREPANCIES I AM NOT PAPERING OVER:

  DETAIL-COUNT = 49, not 33. Your ruling says "your 33-detail measurement". The BirthdayInterview
  account produces 49 assessments today. Either the fixture grew since that number was set, or "33
  details" counted something narrower than assessments. I measured what the fixture actually
  produces and I am telling you the number rather than quietly matching your phrasing.

  I could not include the resolution receipt from the fixtures package on the first attempt -
  `placementResolution` is private[scoring]. That is why PlacementProducerSuite lives in `scoring`.
  I got the numbers via AiCompatibleScores instead, which renders the same resolution.

FULL GATE ON e1c8c40, from last night before the session ended:
  clean compileAll testAll scalafmtCheckAll -- 48 test runs, 4327 tests, 0 failed, 0 error lines,
  CAPTURED_EXIT=0.
